releases.name: v1.9.0 — OpenCode bench 9 → 16
releases.body:
## Heads up if you install via npm

**Your bench grows from 9 personas to 16.** `compliance-reviewer`, `dual-deploy-reviewer`, `executive-sponsor`, `competing-team-lead`, `junior-engineer`, `test-lead`, and `artifact-classifier` all ship to OpenCode now.

These personas have existed in the Claude Code plugin for several releases. `.opencode/build.sh` carried a hand-written `PERSONAS` array that nobody extended when they landed, so OpenCode users have been reviewing with just over half the roster. Output shape is identical either way, which is why a smaller council was invisible.

**What changes for you:** your next review spawns more lanes than your last one. That is slower and it costs more, on your own inference bill. If you are on the `bedrock` preset it bills your AWS account. Nothing is broken and no action is required, but if your review costs jump after upgrading, this is why. Use `--only=` to run a subset.

## Fixed

**Five of the nine personas that were already shipping had broken OpenCode builds.** The build transforms persona files from `agents/` into OpenCode form using prose pattern matching, and each pattern was pinned to the exact line wrapping of the one persona it was written against. Every other wrapping fell through to a catch-all that strips the path but keeps the sentence around it:

| Persona | Shipped with |
|---|---|
| `devils-advocate` | "Read `INPUT.md` at the run directory" — a directory OpenCode does not have |
| `sre` and three others | "Write your scorecard to (removed — filesystem references not used in OpenCode)", which is an instruction to write nowhere |
| four personas | a `persona-metadata/<name>.yml` path the npm package never ships |
| `dual-deploy-reviewer` | its whole Codex delegation section and worked example |

Two source files used `--` where the other twelve used `—`, and that one character was enough to defeat a regex.

The patterns are fixed, but the durable part is a **banned-token gate**: the build now fails if any transformed persona still mentions `$RUN_DIR`, `INPUT.md`, `delegation_request`, `Codex`, or a `persona-metadata/` path. Pattern-matching prose will keep missing new phrasings, so this turns a silent miss into a build failure. It caught all four pre-existing defects the first time it ran.

## Changed

- **`PERSONAS` is derived from `agents/*.md`**, not hand-listed. The roster cannot drift from the Claude Code plugin's again.
- **`agents/AUTHORING.md` moved to `docs/`.** The plugin loader registers every file in `agents/`, so the authoring doc was registering as an agent with no frontmatter. The persona validator no longer skips it by name either: a non-persona file in `agents/` now fails validation rather than being quietly exempted.

## Known issue

`council-chair` still ships with unrewritten filesystem references and is explicitly exempted from the new gate. Its contract is coupled to the run directory in about a dozen places, including `MANIFEST.json`, `personas_run[]`, and the `SYNTHESIS.md.draft` rename. It needs a hand-authored OpenCode variant rather than another substitution, and that is tracked for the next release.

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/astrowicked/devils-council/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

releases.name: v1.8.0 — Per-persona model config + budget preset
releases.body:
Each persona now runs on a right-sized model instead of your session model. Set one env var and the next review puts the Devil's Advocate and Chair on a strong reasoner while cheaper personas run cheap. Defaults apply on install; your own \`opencode.json\` always wins per field.

## Added
- **Per-persona model config (OpenCode)** via \`DEVILS_COUNCIL_MODEL_PRESET\`. Zero-action defaults through the plugin \`config\` hook.
- **\`model_tier\` on every critic** — \`deep-reasoning\` (Devil's Advocate, Chair, Security), \`workhorse\` (Staff/SRE/PM, most bench), \`cheap\` (weak-signal). Lint rule R10 enforces it.
- **Three presets** in \`lib/model-presets.json\`: \`bedrock\` (opus/sonnet/haiku, deep-reasoning gets \`variant: max\`), \`budget\` (all tiers on \`big-pickle\`, near-zero cost), \`cheap\` (free opencode models). Add your own key — no code change.

## Changed
- Plugin migrated to the real \`@opencode-ai/plugin\` function shape (the old shape silently ignored the \`config\` hook). No behavior change to existing hooks.

## Why these model picks
A 30-cell study (5 personas × {opus, sonnet, haiku} × 2 artifacts) plus a non-Anthropic screen (GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, gpt-oss, Gemma, big-pickle) found recall is nearly model-independent, but the real failure mode is **fabrication**. Haiku invented an impossible concurrency bug on the deep-reasoning cells (so did sonnet on one); \`big-pickle\` scored 7.5/9 with none — which is why \`budget\` uses it over haiku.

## Guardrails
- Shipped personas stay **model-silent** (frontmatter would beat \`opencode.json\`); CI fails the build and checks the npm tarball if any persona declares a model.
- Injection is **fail-safe** — a corrupt/missing preset logs one line and every persona falls through to the session model.

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/astrowicked/devils-council/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

releases.name: v1.7.0 — Zero-friction review suggestions
releases.body:
## What's New

**Reviews trigger automatically after planning — no manual invocation needed.**

### GSD Integration (on by default)

After GSD plan-checker completes, you now see:

    [DEVILS-COUNCIL] Plan ready for review. Run:
    /devils-council:review .planning/phases/01-scaffold/01-01-PLAN.md --type=plan
    No additional context needed — the command handles everything.

The agent executes immediately without spending tokens figuring out what to do.

**Breaking change:** `gsd_integration` userConfig default changed from `false` to `true`. Disable with `/plugin config devils-council` if needed.

### Speckit Integration

After `/speckit.plan` completes, the hook detects the plan file path and suggests the exact command:

    [DEVILS-COUNCIL] Plan detected. Run:
    /devils-council:review specs/auth/plan.md --type=plan

Path detection: extracts from tool output, falls back to most-recently-modified `specs/**/plan.md`.

### `/devils-council:review` accepts ANY artifact

Reminder: the core `/review` command is artifact-agnostic. It accepts plans, code diffs, and RFCs from any workflow (GSD, speckit, standalone). The `--type` flag auto-detects if not specified.

## Upgrade

Claude Code: `/plugin uninstall` + `/plugin install` + restart session.
OpenCode: automatic via npm.

## Full Changelog

https://github.com/astrowicked/devils-council/compare/v1.6.1...v1.7.0

releases.name: v1.6.1 — Fix /on-plan shell substitution on macOS/zsh
releases.body:
## Bug Fix

**`/devils-council:on-plan` now works on macOS/zsh** — fixes "Shell command failed for pattern" error.

### Root Cause

Claude Code text-substitutes `$ARGUMENTS` before shell execution, but does NOT recognize `${ARGUMENTS:-}` (brace/default syntax). The `on-plan` command was the only one using this form — all other commands use bare `$ARGUMENTS`.

Result: `PHASE=""` → case match on empty string → exit 2 → "Shell command failed for pattern."

### Fix

Replaced `${ARGUMENTS:-}` with `$ARGUMENTS` in both shell-injection blocks in `commands/on-plan.md`.

### Also included (since v1.6.0)

- Updated GitHub Action section in README (zero-config free tier first)
- Smoke test workflow for GitHub Models API validation

## Upgrade

Claude Code users:

    /plugin uninstall devils-council@devils-council
    /plugin install devils-council@devils-council

OpenCode users: automatic (npm resolves `@latest`).

## Full Changelog

https://github.com/astrowicked/devils-council/compare/v1.6.0...v1.6.1

releases.name: v1.6.0 — Self-eval improvements + persona gap fixes
releases.body:
## What's New

### Self-eval benchmark reaches 100% recall

- **Keyword-bag matching** — `must_claim_contains_any` with OR-logic replaces brittle single-keyword matching in expected findings
- **Run-matching bug fix** — short IDs (e.g., "02") no longer false-match against timestamp substrings in run directory names
- **Provenance documentation** — all 22 expected findings now document their source, the deliberate flaw they target, and when first caught

### Persona prompt improvements

- **SRE** now asks "how do you UNDO this at 3am?" — covers rollback plans, deployment strategy, staged rollouts
- **Devil's Advocate** recognizes circular reasoning (mitigation restates the risk as solved) as a subtype of premise-attack

### CI hardening

- `claude plugin validate` uses exit code instead of grepping stdout for success tokens
- `council-self-review` job skips gracefully when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret is not configured
- Pinned benchmark results excluded from markdown lint

### Positioning reframe

- README: "Get a staff-level LGTM" instead of "Adversarial AI review"
- GitHub Marketplace listing live for the action
- GitHub Discussions enabled for user feedback

## Self-Eval Results

    Recall: 22/22 (100.0%)
    Regressions: 0 blocker, 0 major
    Precision violations: 0
    VERDICT: PASS

## Full Changelog

https://github.com/astrowicked/devils-council/compare/v1.5.2...v1.6.0
